purpose: Model battle mechs and related walkers as boarded, crew-operated, componentized machines that emerge from terrestrial, aerospace, orbital, maritime, subsurface, and industrial robotics. A mech is a physical vehicle and workplace, not a character skin or a single health bar.

evolutionaryPressures.driver: Powered load-bearing frames, hazardous-material work, casualty extraction, logistics and construction.
tradeoffs: operator injury if control loop mismatches body
battery or fuel and cooling burden

evolutionaryPressures.driver: Rough terrain, rubble, steep grades, narrow work sites, manipulator reach and tools that benefit from a high stance.
Mission packages combining protection, sensors, weapons, manipulation and mobility in terrain hostile to wheeled or tracked platforms.
High-altitude, low-pressure, high-wind, toxic or thermally extreme environments.
External station/ship work, assembly, rescue, payload handling and inspection.
Low gravity, dust, vacuum, radiation, cryogenic or chemically hostile environments.
Deep ocean, flooded infrastructure, seabed industry, high pressure and low visibility.
Radiation zones, volcanic/cryogenic sites, collapsed megastructures, unknown biology, high-gravity or unusual material environments.

platformFamilies.name: Utility Exoframe
platformFamilies.crewInterface: motion-harness plus force-sensing grips and foot controls
platformFamilies.signatureTradeoff: agility and access versus payload, endurance and operator fatigue

platformFamilies.name: Light Recon Walker
platformFamilies.crewInterface: seated or suspended pilot rig with hand grips, pedals, displays and safety harness
platformFamilies.signatureTradeoff: speed and low mass versus armor, heat and payload

platformFamilies.name: Combat Walker
platformFamilies.crewInterface: boarded cockpit, motion/force harness, physical controls, tactical displays and manual emergency controls
platformFamilies.signatureTradeoff: firepower and protection versus joint loads, thermal signature, maintenance and recovery burden

platformFamilies.name: Heavy Support Walker
platformFamilies.crewInterface: restrained pilot capsule with assisted motion capture, force-feedback grips and systems panels
platformFamilies.signatureTradeoff: payload and redundancy versus ground pressure, power, transportability and repair time

platformFamilies.name: Orbital Work Mech
platformFamilies.crewInterface: restraint harness, manipulators, hand controllers, suit/vehicle life-support console
platformFamilies.signatureTradeoff: dexterity and reach versus propellant, tether dependence and contamination risk

platformFamilies.name: Environmental Research Walker
platformFamilies.crewInterface: sealed pilot rig with mission-specific tool panels, sensor/logging ports and redundant controls
platformFamilies.signatureTradeoff: instrumentation and survivability versus specialization, mass and supply burden

componentHierarchy.stateCascade: Control input -> pilot/rig state -> control law -> actuator commands -> power/thermal limits -> actual joint forces and contact -> balance/trajectory -> sensor feedback -> pilot correction. Damage and latency propagate through this loop.

rules: grip displacement maps through calibrated control laws
a pilot's fatigue, injury, skill and timing change command quality
keyboard/controller bindings can drive the same virtual grip and visible pilot animation

pilotInterface.movementModel: Do not require the pilot to literally imitate every mech joint. Pilot motion is an input to a control system; the machine's thousands of thrusters or actuators are computed outputs constrained by dynamics, installed components and current damage.
pilotInterface.speedChallenge: A raised/held control posture can demand sustained force or endurance where the vehicle design supports it. Fatigue must emerge from a declared ergonomic/load model, be trainable and equipment-dependent, and never be a universal arbitrary tax.

weaponAndDamageModel.rule: Destroying a weapon mount, actuator, sensor, feed or power bus has a distinct consequence; do not reduce the whole mech to a single hit-point pool.

performanceAndRendering.hypothesis: Visible cost may be bounded by projected pixel coverage, draw/dispatch overhead, geometry/compute workload, memory residency and bandwidth, synchronization, and simulation cost. GPU execution does not make work unlimited.
batchingRules: Join static compatible meshes when profiling shows draw-call/dispatch overhead dominates and the joined asset preserves required material, damage, culling and streaming boundaries.
Do not merge articulated, independently damaged, interactable, independently streamed, or differently animated parts merely to reduce draw calls.
Use GPU instancing for repeated compatible parts; use hierarchical culling and mesh/cluster LOD for large assemblies.
Maintain per-component authoritative simulation state even if visual geometry is merged, instanced, impostored or streamed out.
A visually hidden part can still simulate consequential events at a lower fidelity tier; visual absence does not erase world state.
measuredBudgets: CPU simulation time per active actor and background actor
GPU memory resident/committed and streaming churn
scalabilityStrategy: Define target hardware tiers and test scenes before claiming a population scale.
Use adaptive fidelity tiers for near interaction, combat, tactical simulation and strategic/background history.
Keep persistent world and component state separate from render caches.
Profile representative worst cases: many articulated mechs, damage, smoke, lights, transparent guidance ghosts, cockpit screens and simultaneous combat.

If bottleneck is draw-call overhead, batch/instance; if bandwidth, reduce data movement and improve locality; if memory, stream and compress; if pixel/fill, reduce overdraw/resolution or simplify shading; if CPU simulation, reduce update frequency or model detail without erasing consequences.
falsifiableHypotheses: If cost is primarily pixel-limited, reducing render resolution should improve GPU frame time predictably.
If draw-call/dispatch overhead dominates, compatible batching or instancing should improve frame time without unacceptable culling/damage regressions.
If memory bandwidth dominates, reducing per-frame uploads and improving residency should improve frame time.
If simulation dominates, lowering pixel count alone will not solve the frame-time problem.
performanceAndRendering.noUnlimitedClaim: Performance ceilings remain. Pixel coverage is one dimension; memory capacity, bandwidth, bus transfer, cache locality, command submission, synchronization, geometry processing, physics and simulation all matter.

validationGates: Mechs are boarded vehicles with visible pilot occupancy and physical controls.
Every mech function maps to installed systems and components.
Pilot input is not identical to actuator output; control laws and physical limits intervene.
Fatigue depends on ergonomic demand and pilot state.
Distinct environment families have credible life-support, locomotion, power, thermal and recovery requirements.
Damage affects specific components and cascades through dependencies.
GPU/CPU/memory/bus hypotheses are tested with benchmarks rather than asserted.
Visual mesh merging never destroys component identity or damage simulation.
Performance tests include both pixel-heavy and simulation-heavy scenes.
Illustrative families do not silently lock faction identity or balance.
